subject.title: fix: block unsafe workspace dotenv controls [AI]

question: Should the expanded workspace dotenv denylist be accepted as the intended compatibility boundary after real proof confirms that trusted shell/global dotenv sources remain usable for the same controls?
rationale: The change deliberately alters which existing repository-local configuration is honored at a security-sensitive trust boundary; tests enumerate intended names but cannot decide the acceptable upgrade contract.

options.title: Require boundary proof before merge
options.body: Request a redacted terminal or runtime-log demonstration of a blocked workspace control and preserved trusted-source behavior, then review the intended compatibility impact.

options.title: Accept the compatibility change
options.body: Merge after maintainer confirmation that affected repository-local dotenv controls are intentionally unsupported regardless of the missing live proof.

options.title: Narrow the protected surface
options.body: Reduce the new blocklist to controls with explicit trust-boundary contracts if maintainers do not want to change all listed workspace configurations.

recommendation.title: Require boundary proof before merge
recommendation.body: Request a redacted terminal or runtime-log demonstration of a blocked workspace control and preserved trusted-source behavior, then review the intended compatibility impact.

likelyOwner.reason: The contributor can provide the missing after-fix proof and clarify the tested environment; maintainer confirmation remains required for the permanent boundary.
